extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It combines 28 existing multimodal datasets with 3 newly created datasets and includes 6,141 examples across diverse visual and mathematical tasks.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was built by collecting multiple source datasets in multimodal settings: nine MathQA datasets, 19 publicly available VQA datasets with math-related instances, and three newly introduced datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). For the VQA datasets, the authors first used heuristic rules to automatically select likely mathematical examples, then had three expert annotators manually label them, and resolved disagreements through majority voting and discussion. For the new datasets, questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a review process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Publicly available MathQA and VQA source datasets containing math-related instances, plus puzzle test figures from online learning platforms and academic illustrations/tables/figures/charts from online education resources and papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: August 2023 (for the PaperQA source papers); no broader collection dates specified
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were trained with detailed instructions and examples to label whether a problem involves mathematical reasoning, using three options: Yes, No, or Unsure; they could also leave comments if anything was incorrect or offensive. The paper also mentions an annotation tool for expert annotators and inter-annotator agreement analysis among three annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: An annotation tool / GUI was developed for labeling mathematical reasoning; for the Multimodal Bard assessment task, a screenshot of the AMT worker interface is mentioned.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement was evaluated using Fleiss Kappa among three annotators, yielding a score of 0.775, indicating substantial agreement.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Expert annotators; no further demographic details are provided.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark may have coverage gaps in certain types of mathematical problems and visuals, and its annotations come from heterogeneous original data providers with non-unified formats and structures.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Coverage is incomplete for some problem/visual types; scalability and generalizability to other domains are concerns; only 85.6% of examples have annotations; annotations are heterogeneous and lack a unified format; future work aims to refine data noise and expand coverage.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve understanding and enhancement of AI capabilities in mathematical and visual reasoning, with ongoing maintenance and leaderboard updates in response to community feedback and new models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking/evaluating model performance on mathematical and visual reasoning tasks; future iterations aim to broaden problem and visual coverage and provide unified annotations. The study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process; maintainers commit to refining data noise in response to community feedback and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To ensure that each source dataset is well represented in testmini and to maintain a distribution in testmini closely resembling the whole set, we adopted this sampling strategy: (1) first, randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset; (2) then, randomly sample the remaining questions for each source dataset on their proportion in the entire set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For non-math-targeted VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates; examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words were selected. These examples were then manually labeled by expert annotators, and majority voting was used to finalize the collection. The dataset was also quality-checked.
